core.title: Order present header fields as URN -> Tested-By -> Runtime -> Purpose
core.given: A file inside the stack's scan scope carries a URN traceability field plus any of Tested-By, Runtime, Purpose
core.when: the file exists in the checked codebase, regardless of whether its header was edited in the current change
core.then: The present header fields MUST appear in the order URN -> Tested-By -> Runtime -> Purpose.
prefer: During GREEN repair: reorder only the header lines needed to restore the canonical sequence.
During GREEN repair: keep the existing field values unless another convention proves one is wrong.
During GREEN repair: preserve unrelated comments.
avoid: Do not broaden: rewriting identifiers, acceptance bindings, runtime, or purpose merely while fixing order.
Do not broaden: moving implementation code to satisfy a header-order finding.
Adding a missing field just to silence this rule — absence is each field's own rule, not this one.
unless: The file has no URN — it is skipped; there is nothing to order against.
A field is absent — it is not considered; presence is each field's own rule.
Other comment lines are interleaved between the fields — this is allowed.
core.why: A fixed order (identity, then proof, then execution context, then intent — each field answering the question the previous one raises) lets a reader, human or tool, know where to look without parsing; the order is identical in every realization of this convention.
evidence: Prove: the present header fields appear in canonical order (the stack's header-order check reports no finding).
Prove: the current behavioral acceptance still passes after the reorder.
The order fix touches only header lines and moves no implementation code; field values are unchanged except where another convention proves a value wrong.
verification: Canonical order: URN -> Tested-By -> Runtime -> Purpose.
The check collects the line numbers of the header fields that are present and reports the first field that appears before its predecessor.
A present field is a header field the file actually carries; absent fields are skipped so this rule never double-reports a missing field another rule owns.
Files with no URN are skipped entirely.
Non-field comment lines interleaved between the fields are ignored.
Severity 2; disposition strict: fail on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

The check covers every file in the profile's scan scope that carries a URN field; it is not gated on edits, phase or prior findings — a header-order finding confirms a violation but is not a precondition for the obligation.

fires: A file in the checked scope carries a URN field and its Tested-By field appears above the URN field.
A file in the checked scope has URN, Runtime and Purpose fields with Purpose written before Runtime, even if the header was not touched in the current change.
The check reports a header-order finding on a file.
doesNotFire: A file with no URN field at all (nothing to order against).
A file whose header lacks Tested-By or Runtime but whose present fields are in canonical order (missing fields belong to their own rules).
A file whose present fields are in canonical order with other comment lines interleaved between them.

profileRequirements.meaning: The set of files this rule's check covers: every file in the stack's scan scope is checked for header order, not only edited files; bun.json fixes no narrower scan set than 'the checked codebase'.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file's traceability header fields (URN, Tested-By, Runtime, Purpose) are written in this stack, so the content-scan observer can recognize which fields are present and on which lines.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a content scan for the URN, Tested-By, Runtime and Purpose fields (activation.facts[0].note)

neutralityNotes: The four field names and the canonical order are convention-level (identical across realizations), so they stay verbatim in the core; only their concrete syntax and the observer that scans for them are profile concerns (proposed key urn.header#header_fields; observability needs_new_observer). 'It is the same order in Python, Vite and Bun' was neutralized to 'identical in every realization of this convention' without weakening the claim. fires/doesNotFire were neutralized by replacing 'Bun-checked file' with 'file in the checked scope' and 'the detector' with 'the check'. Severity 2 and the strict disposition are per-rule facts kept in core:verification; the shared-node id and its Bun-specific wording stay with the realization. Detector and finding ids (bun_green_traceability_detector, GREEN-HEADER-004, BUN-GREEN-HEADER-ORDER-001) are bunOnly. bun.json fixes no concrete scan set beyond 'the checked codebase', so the core takes the file scope from roots.scan rather than inventing one.
